senses.definition: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords; the sound thus produced.
examples: I spoke in a near whisper.

quotes.text: "Now, look here, Jim Hawkins," he said, in a steady whisper, that was no more than audible.

examples: There are whispers of rebellion all around.

senses.definition: (figurative) A faint trace or hint (of something).
examples: The soup had just a whisper of basil.

senses.definition: A low rustling sound, like that of the wind in leaves.

senses.definition: (occult) A projection of intention and influence caused by sending thoughts or desires outward through softly-spoken words or subtle mental or energetic means.

quotes.text: "Witches feel that anyone who is against them has to be destroyed. The method is to give the victim what we call a whispering. It is similar to the aborigine ceremony in Australia of singing someone to death. The witches gather in a circle and focus their hate on the persons they have in mind. These vibrations from their minds and voices carry whispers to the one who they are working against."
quotes.reference: 1965, Attila Zohar, Kings Cross Black Magic, Sydney: Horwitz Publications, page 66:

senses.definition: (intransitive) To speak softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter words without sonant breath; to talk without that vibration of the vocal cords which gives sonorous, or vocal, sound.

quotes.text:
I can hear them whisper as we pass by
It's a bad sign, bad sign
